task.description:
Read ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis in full at handoffs/WF03-ISS0451-20260904/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json (result.summary) -- it confirmed empirically (real code read plus a live throwaway probe) that a PERSISTENT Poller fault cascades from Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' own budget exhaustion (max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60) into the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's default OTP restart budget (3 restarts / 5 seconds, never overridden in lib/letflow/application.ex) within about 96ms wall-clock, taking down the whole application (Repo, Bandit included) -- the exact incident REQ-219 exists to prevent, just for a persistent rather than single-shot fault.

Produce a design artefact in lib/letflow/design/ (follow this project's existing convention, e.g. lib/letflow/design/req219-supervision-layering.md's shape) choosing and fully specifying a fix. ISS-0451's own description names two candidate options, neither prescribed: (a) raise the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own restart intensity so it tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle without exiting itself, and/or (b) give Pollers a circuit-breaker/backoff so a persistent fault degrades to a stopped-but-not-crash-looping state rather than repeatedly re-exhausting its own budget and repeatedly costing the top level a restart. You choose the design -- this is a real architectural decision with an availability tradeoff (see the design considerations below), not a default to pick without reasoning.

Design considerations to work through and document (this is what ISS-0451's AC2 requires -- concrete arithmetic, not just a chosen number):
- If you raise the top-level's restart intensity alone: what value tolerates at least one full Pollers-exhaustion-and-restart cycle (Pollers' own 5-in-60s budget means Pollers can legitimately exit and be restarted by the top level at most once per 60s under NORMAL bounded-transient-fault operation before Pollers' own budget resets -- but under a PERSISTENT fault, Pollers re-exhausts almost immediately after each restart, so the top level would need to tolerate MANY such Pollers-exits within its own window, not just one, unless something also slows the retry rate). State the exact max_restarts/max_seconds you choose for the top level and show the arithmetic for why it survives a persistent fault indefinitely (or for how long, if not indefinitely) rather than merely surviving one extra restart.
- If you add a circuit-breaker/backoff to Pollers instead (or in addition): what state machine, what backoff schedule, what makes it degrade to 'stopped, not crash-looping' rather than continuing to consume top-level restart budget at all. Consider that Pollers currently holds TWO independently-gated poller GenServers as peers (Letflow.Scheduler.Poller and Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller) -- a circuit-breaker design must state whether it applies per-poller or to the whole Pollers supervisor, and why.
- Whichever you choose (or if you choose both), the design must not weaken REQ-219's own AC2 (boot-order: Infrastructure before Pollers, structural via list order) or AC4 (single-crash isolation: Pollers exhausting its budget once must still leave Infrastructure/Http alone) -- state explicitly how your design preserves both.
- The design must specify exactly what test(s) TEST-DESIGNER will need to write: a regression test simulating a PERSISTENT Poller fault (never cleared, unlike REQ-219's AC4 test) proving Letflow.Supervisor (top-level), Letflow.Repo, and the Bandit listener all remain alive after Pollers repeatedly exhausts its budget -- name the exact mechanism the test will use to keep the fault persistent (a test-only flag, following the existing force_poller_crash precedent in pollers_test.exs, or something else) and what observable proves the top-level supervisor never exited (e.g. Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor) staying the same pid, or a monitor).

This is a design artefact ONLY -- no implementation code, no .ex file changes outside lib/letflow/design/. Signatures/specs/config-value choices only, per this project's design-vs-implementation convention (see CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria, which will check for implementation code present and fail the gate if found).
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact created under lib/letflow/design/, named appropriately (e.g. iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md)
Design states the exact top-level restart-intensity value chosen (if that lever is used) with the arithmetic showing it tolerates at least one full Pollers-budget-exhaustion cycle, per ISS-0451 AC2
Design states the exact circuit-breaker/backoff mechanism (if that lever is used) with its state machine and thresholds
Design explicitly confirms REQ-219 AC2 (boot order) and AC4 (single-crash isolation) are preserved and states why
Design specifies the exact test mechanism and observable(s) for the new persistent-fault regression test
No implementation code (.ex function bodies) present in the design document -- signatures/specs/config values only

result.summary: Design artefact written: lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md. Read ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis (step-01) in full and treated its empirically-probed arithmetic (top level OTP-default 3/5, Pollers 5/60, persistent fault re-exhausts Pollers every ~24-30ms, top level exits at 96ms wall-clock across 4 Pollers-level exits) as verified measurement per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 1.1, not re-derived from scratch. Worked the arithmetic one step further than the diagnosis did (design section 1): raising the top level's own max_restarts to ANY finite N only delays, never prevents, an identical cascade under a truly persistent fault, because nothing about a larger N changes the ~10-50ms re-exhaustion RATE Pollers experiences -- rate is the binding constraint, and only a mechanism that changes Pollers' own retry rate (a circuit breaker) can make the top level survive indefinitely rather than merely longer. This settled the choice: DESIGN CHOSEN = both levers, not as equal partners. (1) PRIMARY FIX -- a circuit-breaker in a new sibling process, Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker (GenServer, 4th top-level child, listed after Pollers and before Http so REQ-219 AC2's Infrastructure-before-Pollers ordering is untouched), monitoring Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers and requiring TWO consecutive :DOWN events (not one) before tripping :closed -> :open -- the two-event threshold is what keeps REQ-219's own already-passing AC4 single-shot test unaffected, since that test's fault is cleared after exactly one :DOWN. On the 2nd consecutive :DOWN the breaker calls Supervisor.terminate_child/2 on Pollers (stopped, not crash-looping -- ISS-0451's own required end state), then backs off on an exponential schedule (1s / 5s / 30s / 2m / 5m-cap) before each :half_open retry probe, resetting the trip counter only on a genuine recovery. Applies per-Pollers-supervisor (not per-individual-poller), consistent with REQ-219's own already-accepted 'both pollers restart together' consequence, now extended to 'both stop together.' (2) DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH ONLY, not the fix itself -- raise the top-level Letflow.Supervisor's own max_restarts from the OTP default 3 to 5 (max_seconds stays 5, unchanged). Arithmetic: the breaker's own worst-case top-level consumption is exactly 2 restarts (the 1st :DOWN that starts observation, the 2nd that trips the breaker and is immediately followed by terminate_child, so no 3rd automatic restart is ever attempted) -- 5 minus that 2 restores exactly the OTP default's original 3-restart margin, now available for a genuinely UNRELATED transient Infrastructure/Http restart landing in the same 5-second window as a persistent-Poller-fault episode, which the bare default would leave zero margin for. Explicitly justified as small (2, not 50) so it does not erode REQ-219 decision 3's own correctness property that a crash-looping Infrastructure/Http child must still take the app down. Design section 5 confirms both REQ-219 AC2 (Infrastructure still listed and started first; PollersBreaker's own init only names-looks-up Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, no dependency on list position beyond being listed after it) and AC4 (the breaker's two-consecutive-:DOWN threshold means it never intervenes during REQ-219's own existing single-shot AC4 test) are preserved, with the exact reasoning for why neither existing test needs modification. Design section 6 specifies the regression test test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs: reuses the EXISTING force_poller_crash/start_scheduler double-gated seam verbatim (no new gate, no new config key) but -- the deliberate inverse of REQ-219's own AC4 test -- never clears force_poller_crash mid-test, making the fault genuinely persistent; observables are a Process.monitor on the top-level Letflow.Supervisor pid (primary, catches a fast exit-and-respawn a single before/after whereis could miss) plus a pid-equality check (confirming), both asserted TRUE while the fault is still active and the breaker is still :open, alongside Repo/Infrastructure/Http pid-unchanged assertions; a new plain (non-double-gated) public accessor Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker.breaker_state/0 is specified as the one new test-observability surface, justified in section 6.3 as not needing the compile-time test-hook gate since it only reads state and cannot alter production behavior. No implementation code anywhere in the doc -- module/function signatures, @type shapes, a state-transition table, and prose only, matching req219-supervision-layering.md's own established shape. Three open questions recorded explicitly rather than silently resolved (section 7): whether the regression test must exercise a full backoff cycle or only the initial trip; the exact log message wording; and whether the breaker process's own crash-recovery is explicitly test-verified (believed safe -- ordinary child of the now-5-restart top-level budget, resumes :closed on restart -- but not empirically probed the way section 1's core cascade was).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate this design (WF-03 Step 2b/next), per the workflow's producer/validator pairing -- verify all 6 of this handoff's own acceptance criteria are met (artefact path/name, top-level intensity arithmetic per AC2, circuit-breaker state machine/thresholds, REQ-219 AC2/AC4 preservation stated explicitly, exact test mechanism/observables specified, and confirm no implementation code -- only signatures/specs/config values -- is present anywhere in the 500+ line document, particularly the GenServer state-shape/handle_info signature-level descriptions in section 3.4, which describe callback CONTRACTS and transition logic in prose, not function bodies).
